## Outcome
Every mutating pm action leaves a permanent, tamper-evident record. Any item is restorable to any recorded version. A third party holding only an exported proof bundle can confirm the recorded history was never altered.

## Standing invariant this closes
The product invariant states that all mutating actions record permanently and immutably. Today item mutations satisfy it; workspace-scoped mutations (pm-klo8) do not, the completeness gate proving it (pm-9yfo) is not built, portable proof (pm-3z0k) is not exported, and authorship (pm-u14c) is self-asserted.

## Delivery chain
pm-9yfo completeness gate (phase 1 item scope first) -> pm-klo8 workspace audit stream -> pm-3z0k portable attestation -> pm-u14c per-entry signatures. Compaction, redaction, and repair paths must each be proven not to break replay.

## Explicit non-goals
No history rewriting to fix legacy gaps. No hand-attribution of legacy unknown-author events.
Outcome milestone: provable history — every mutation immutably recorded, independently verifiable, restorable to any version

A contract-driven gate proves every mutating CLI and SDK action appends a history entry, with zero exemptions outside a reviewed waiver ledger; Workspace-scoped mutations (schema/config/profile/init) write to an append-only audit stream; A detached hash-chain proof bundle exports and verifies standalone, without the workspace; Per-entry author attribution is verifiable rather than self-asserted, and unknown-author events are rejected under strict mode; Restore-to-any-version and point-in-time reads hold across compaction, redaction, repair, and merge
Any third party can verify that the recorded history of any workspace was never altered, and any item can be reconstructed at any point in time
Immutable, verifiable proof is what makes an agent-written tracker trustworthy: without it, thousands of autonomous mutations are unauditable assertions.
Precondition for organizational adoption, for policy enforcement, and for any regulated or contractual use of pm as the system of record.
Zero mutating actions bypass the history stream, per-entry authorship is attributable, and a detached proof bundle verifies standalone.
Workspace-scoped mutations (schema, config, profile, init) still leave no append-only record, so the every-mutation-leaves-proof invariant is not yet true.

value.text:
Provable-history architecture

Authoritative history is an append-only event system covering item state, workspace configuration/schema/profile state, relationship changes, package activation, release attribution, and audited maintenance. Every event records schema version, operation contract id, actor provenance, timestamp source, causal/base version, patch or domain payload, before/after hashes, and chain algorithm identifier.

Integrity is layered: per-stream hash chains detect local alteration; workspace manifests commit stream heads; detached proof bundles permit independent verification; optional transparency-log or signed-release anchors make later history replacement detectable outside the repository. Algorithm agility and format migrations are explicit so decades-long proofs do not depend on one hash forever.

Restore is a projection, never a destructive rewrite of proof. Point-in-time reads replay from verified snapshots plus events. Compaction emits a verifiable checkpoint linked to the pruned prefix. Redaction, repair, and legal erasure append auditable transformation evidence with policy authority and preserve the maximum proof permitted. Verification gates enumerate every mutating CLI, SDK, MCP, and package action from contracts and require an event or a reviewed, shrinking waiver.
